title: Cold rebuild: The weekly report
summary: Rebuild The weekly report from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **The weekly report** in *Aggregation and axis*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.title: Rebuild The weekly report cold
prompt: `sales` is a 2-D float array (stores x days) that may contain `np.nan` for days a store did
not report. Write `report(sales)` returning a dict:
- `"total"`: the grand total of all known sales, rounded to 1 decimal,
- `"best_store"`: index of the store with the highest total (ignoring gaps),
- `"worst_day"`: index of the day with the lowest **average** across stores (ignoring gaps),
All values must be plain Python numbers (`float`/`int`).
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
